title: Ionic Memory and Computing
intro: We investigate how ion interactions and local free-energy barriers allow a nanopore to retain that history. Molecular simulations connect the motion of individual ions to changes in conductance and the response to successive voltage pulses.
caption: Biological signaling, artificial neural networks, and ionic devices that reproduce aspects of neuronal function.
background_html: An ion-conducting pore can respond differently to the same voltage depending on its electrical history. This memory offers a way to reproduce aspects of synaptic behavior with ions, the charge carriers used in biological signaling.

title: Selective Ion Transport
intro: Biological ion channels provide examples of selective, rapid transport. We examine how pore chemistry and membrane motion change the barriers to ion passage, including how small chemical differences can separate ions with similar properties.
caption: Ion-channel-inspired membrane concepts for separating rare-earth ions.
background_html: A membrane must distinguish between ions while still allowing them to pass. Strong binding can favor one ion over another, but it can also slow the release of the captured ion. This tension matters for water purification and the recovery of valuable elements.

title: Interfacial Molecular Recognition
intro: Our molecular simulations follow the motion of surface-bound biomolecules and their interactions with the electrode and surrounding solution. In collaboration with experimental researchers, we examine how these interfacial effects influence recognition and electrochemical sensing.
caption: Target recognition by biological receptors and by receptors attached to sensing electrodes.
background_html: Attaching a molecular receptor to an electrode changes its environment. A receptor that binds a target in solution may adopt a different shape or encounter different molecules at the surface, changing how it recognizes the target.
